clue.text: Performance cancelled for egotist

parts.note: a show is a performance on stage
an event called off is cancelled

explanation.surface: A show is scrapped because of its self-obsessed star.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off is someone who flaunts themselves, a vain self-promoter, much like an egotist.

clue.text: Reaper touring Santa's home disheartened, having little time for fun

indicators.note: the reaper's tool goes round the other pieces, as a tourer circles a place

parts.note: a sickle is the reaper's blade, here standing for the reaper

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letter of the place name is dropped

parts.note: Lapland is where Father Christmas traditionally lives
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Death with his scythe glumly visits Father Christmas's homeland, short of time for enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' drops the middle letter, giving LAPAND, and 'touring' puts it and T inside the sickle. Slap and tickle is British slang for playful kissing and cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap and tickle is informal British slang for amorous horseplay, light-hearted canoodling, a kind of fun.

clue.text: In deep water, delivering impure cocaine

indicators.note: impure cocaine is adulterated, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drug runner, in trouble, hands over cut cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In deep water' looks like the idiom for being in trouble, but read literally it means out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic describes what belongs to or lives in the ocean, so in deep sea water.

clue.text: Old shift from which monthly release scheduled?

parts.note: to shift is to change or vary

explanation.surface: An old roster change sets out when the monthly release comes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the monthly release is an egg released in ovulation.
explanation.definitionFit: The ovary releases an egg each month in the menstrual cycle, a fanciful description of the organ.

clue.text: The cow puts Scotsman in boiling oil!

parts.note: to cook something in boiling oil is to fry it; 'puts ... in' frames the act
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A gruesome punishment: someone dumps a Scot into a pan of boiling oil.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'puts Scotsman in boiling oil' as fries Ian: FRIES then IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Friesian is a breed of black-and-white dairy cattle, so an example of a cow.

clue.text: Married man (English) married woman (French)

parts.note: Adam was the first man

explanation.surface: A list entry contrasting an English husband with a French wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs.

clue.text: Bird taking issue with food

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a mag
a pie is an item of food

explanation.surface: Someone objects to what is on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking issue' suggests disagreeing; here issue is a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white crow-family species, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Bomb drawing complaint

parts.note: a doodle is an idle drawing
a bug is a minor illness or complaint

explanation.surface: A grumble about a terrible sketch, as if it bombed.
explanation.walkthrough: The doodlebug was the V-1 flying bomb sent against Britain in 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodlebug was the wartime nickname for the German V-1 flying bomb.

clue.text: 007's boss gets 007, perhaps, a fuchsia

parts.note: M is James Bond's chief in the spy novels
James Bond is an example of a secret agent

explanation.surface: James Bond's chief presents him with a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuchsia is a vivid purplish-red colour, essentially the shade also called magenta.

clue.text: State getting on with evening out

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
someone getting on in years is aging

explanation.surface: Someone declares that they are growing old as the night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' looks like a night on the town; it means making level.
explanation.definitionFit: Averaging means levelling values out to a mean, so smoothing or evening things out.

clue.text: Good books inspire word of revulsion, or anything?

annotationWithheld.why: Good books inspire word of revulsion, or anything? (5): OT round UGH gives OUGHT with 'anything' as definition, but 'Good' has no job, and no source gives a parse using it
annotationWithheld.clue: Good books inspire word of revulsion, or anything?

clue.text: Of all the monks, a Trappist's remit — and that's an understatement!

definitions.text: Of all the monks, a Trappist's remit
definitions.meaning: Trappist monks keep a near-total vow of silence, so their remit is to speak less than any other order
a stock phrase signalling that something is far stronger than just said

explanation.surface: A remark on silent monks, admitting this barely covers it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: of all monks, Trappists have the duty to utter the least.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a set idiom admitting understatement, and literally describes a silent monk's rule.

clue.text: Upset, during the year of victory at last

parts.note: anno is Latin for in the year, as in Anno Domini

indicators.note: the final letter of the word victory is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed during a year that ended in triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to irritate or bother them, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Vehicles veer across the motorway?

definitions.meaning: aircraft fitted with skis for landing on snow
read as two words, to jump from one traffic lane to another

explanation.surface: Cars swerve dangerously across a fast road.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SKIP LANES, the answer describes erratic driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski-planes are aircraft with skis, vehicles; and skip lanes is what reckless drivers do.

clue.text: GP gets senior citizen on to American programme

indicators.note: the pensioner is placed onto, so after, the American abbreviation

parts.note: a general practitioner is a doctor, a doc
OAP is the British abbreviation for old age pensioner

explanation.surface: A family doctor helps a pensioner get onto an American TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A docusoap is a television documentary series following real people, a type of programme.

clue.text: Very proper, men having a legal adviser

parts.note: so is an intensifier meaning very
licit means lawful or proper
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A very correct gentleman with a lawyer on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is a British lawyer who advises clients, a kind of legal adviser.

clue.text: Religious office, group seeking extremes of celibacy

parts.note: Abba was the Swedish pop group

indicators.note: the outer letters, first and last, of the word celibacy are taken

explanation.surface: A church post is sought by a band in search of chastity.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbacy is the office or term of an abbot, a religious post.

clue.text: Magic word's construction process

parts.note: both how a spell is cast, uttering a magic word, and how letters are put together to form any word

explanation.surface: A wizard explains how an incantation is put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelling is forming words letter by letter, and casting a spell is spelling in another sense.

clue.text: One having power to transfix man — do it!

definitions.text: One having power to transfix man — do it!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the power letter pierces the word for man, sitting inside it

parts.note: a male is a man

explanation.surface: An order to someone with the power to run a man through.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: the P transfixes MALE, as one with power impales a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or transfix with a sharp stake, as the clue commands.

clue.text: Aristocracy always in the paper

indicators.note: the word for always goes inside the sheet

parts.note: a page is a sheet of paper
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: The nobility is forever featuring in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of peers, the nobility, a synonym for aristocracy.

clue.text: Quotation with which European swine hit hard

parts.note: a swine is a pig
to rap is to hit sharply
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A saying a European uses to strike a pig hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is a quotation set at the start of a book or chapter.

clue.text: Wild animal beginning to eat children's author

indicators.note: the first letter of the word eat is taken

explanation.surface: A savage beast starts eating a writer for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges ANIMAL to AAMILN, then E ends it. A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh books, so he is a children's author.

clue.text: Left turn cuts bend at regular intervals

indicators.note: every second letter of the words turn, cuts, bend is taken

explanation.surface: A driving instruction: turn left where the road bends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction for the turn; it means not used.
explanation.definitionFit: Left means remaining or not taken, the same as unused.

clue.text: Close to Denmark, alliance constructed waterway

indicators.note: the close, or last letter, of the word Denmark is taken
the letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A coalition near Denmark builds a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like it means near Denmark, but it picks that word's last letter; 'constructed' then rearranges the letters of the alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kiel Canal is a German ship canal linking the North Sea and Baltic, a waterway.

clue.text: African transport appeared impractical, ultimately

parts.note: came means turned up or appeared

indicators.note: the final letter of the word impractical is taken

explanation.surface: A form of travel in Africa turned out to be unworkable in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels are used across North Africa for carrying people and goods, a form of transport.

clue.text: Provide for some picnic, a terrine

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bring food for a picnic, including a pâté.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater for is to provide food or supplies, a synonym for provide.

clue.text: Former stage routine far from improvised?

parts.note: ex means former
an act is a performer's routine on stage

explanation.surface: An old stage turn that was anything but ad-libbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise, the opposite of something made up on the spot, so far from improvised.

clue.text: To wit, where shopkeeper's money kept, a little bit

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for namely or to wit
a shopkeeper keeps money in the till

explanation.surface: Namely, a small sum sits in the shop's cash drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark, a little bit of something.

clue.text: Become furious, as diocese embarrassed

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
embarrassed people go red in the face

explanation.surface: A bishop's district is angered and red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming very angry, so to become furious.

clue.text: Chap covers limb with such an item?

definitions.text: Chap covers limb with such an item?

indicators.note: the chap's word goes round the limb's word, covering it

parts.note: a gent is a chap
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A man covers his arm with a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: ARM is covered by GENT, as a chap covers a limb with clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is an item of clothing, which a man might use to cover his arm.
